body: xref: https://github.com/rapidsai/docker/issues/857#issuecomment-4007485052 for how to trigger this bug with conda + Jupyter notebook.

Short-term - If `CONDA_PREFIX` is undefined, falling back to `sys.prefix` works well. Have submitted this change as a PR: https://github.com/cupy/cupy/pull/9781

Should add have confirmed this fixes the issue with unactivated Conda environments

<hr>

Longer term - Think it would be worth looking at this logic and streamlining it more around using `sys.prefix` regardless of environments. That would likely help make this easier to test and maintain in a variety of cases

Would be happy to discuss this further 🙂

In fact if I check 

```python
import os                                                                                                             
print("CONDA_PREFIX:", os.environ.get('CONDA_PREFIX'))

from cupy._environment import _get_conda_cuda_path, _get_include_dir_from_conda_or_wheel, get_cuda_path               
print("conda cuda path:", _get_conda_cuda_path())
print("cuda path:", get_cuda_path())                                                                                  
print("include dirs:", _get_include_dir_from_conda_or_wheel(12, 4))
```

```
#showing it the fix doesn't work
CONDA_PREFIX: None
conda cuda path: None
cuda path: /anaconda/envs/rapids/lib/python3.13/lib-dynload/..
include dirs: []
```

In a system where  `CONDA_PREFIX` is not propagated to the Jupyter kernel even though the conda env is  active.                                                        
                                                             
Looking at `_environment.py` I think what happens is: 
                     
 1. `_get_conda_cuda_path()` returns `None` (PR fix behavior) — but no fallback exists for finding the CUDA path when  
 `CONDA_PREFIX` is missing. At least the current implementation doesn't work
 2. `_get_include_dir_from_conda_or_wheel()` returns `[]` — it tries `_get_conda_cuda_path()` (gets `None`), then tries     
 `find_nvidia_header_directory('cudart')` (also fails) — so no CUDA include path is passed to NVRTC.           
 3. `get_cuda_path()` returns an unresolved path — nvrtc is found via system-search at
 `/anaconda/envs/rapids/lib/python3.13/lib-dynload/../../libnvrtc.so.12`, and `os.path.dirname` is applied twice without  
 resolving .., giving `/anaconda/envs/rapids/lib/python3.13/lib-dynload/`

 **End result:** NVRTC compiles without the CUDA include directory → `cuda_fp16.h` not found → `NVRTC_ERROR_COMPILATION`.

For reference, this run with no problems when I run this on the terminal where the environment is activated and a `CONDA_PREFIX` is set.

Re-pening as per offline discussion with Naty for tracking.  Seems that the environment in question is weird enough that the fix was not sufficient.

(I am unsure right now whether the bigger thing might be in `cuda-pathfinder` or even if the environment there is just really strange, but if e.g. `cuda-pathfinder` starts defaulting to guess `sys.prefix` for the `CONDA_PREFIX` we should follow in CuPy.)

Discussed internally. Let me close this issue. 

I am not convinced this is a bug on the CuPy side. We need more info to diagnose. Look at the new error from the err log:
```c++
/anaconda/envs/rapids/lib/python3.13/site-packages/cupy/_core/include/cupy/float16.cuh(19): catastrophic error: cannot open source file "cuda_fp16.h"
  #include <cuda_fp16.h>
```
This is not a symptom that we have seen so far. Something is wrong with this test env.

CuPy’s transition to the pathfinder is half done, so we still have some internal logic that assembles the header paths:
- here https://github.com/cupy/cupy/blob/8cd2faaacf383db4fc66b0318cf474edf0b8332f/cupy/_core/core.pyx#L2532
- which calls 
https://github.com/cupy/cupy/blob/8cd2faaacf383db4fc66b0318cf474edf0b8332f/cupy/_environment.py#L591 
to get the path to CUDA headers, including fp16
- which now correctly skips the situation when `CONDA_PREFIX` is not set (PR #9779) https://github.com/cupy/cupy/blob/8cd2faaacf383db4fc66b0318cf474edf0b8332f/cupy/_environment.py#L600

If no include path is found, the path finding would have raised a Python exception, instead of letting it go all the way to NVRTC and hit a compiler error.

I suggested offline that if we still have the problematic env ready to run, set the env var `CUPY_DUMP_CUDA_SOURCE_ON_ERROR=1`, re-run the reproducer, and see if it dumps the compiler options passed to NVRTC for us to debug. Once we gather this info, feel free to file a new bug.

In the meanwhile, @jayavenkatesh19 reported that the RAPIDS team has found a way to activate the conda env in the container, and `CONDA_PREFIX` is now correctly set. So this is no longer a blocker. That said, I'd still love to get to the bottom of the new error.
